root_cause.text: `__rdma_block_iter_next()` in the RDMA umem/block iterator used 32-bit `unsigned int` temporaries to reassemble DMA segments from IOMMU-linearized scatter-gather entries, so block offsets and deltas truncated for mappings ≥4G and produced incorrect DMA addresses.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `block_offset` and `delta` in `drivers/infiniband/core/iter.c` from `unsigned int` to `dma_addr_t`, and the CVE/commit message states that “it is overflowing the 32 bit stack values and computed the wrong DMA addresses for blocks after the truncation” when large blocks are split across multiple SG entries.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use dma_addr_t for block offset calculations to avoid address truncation in RDMA block iteration.
intent_record.what: In __rdma_block_iter_next(), the local variables block_offset and delta were changed from unsigned int to dma_addr_t.
intent_record.how: This changes the arithmetic and storage used for block iteration offsets to match DMA address sizing, preventing truncation or overflow when handling large DMA addresses on platforms where dma_addr_t is wider than unsigned int.

grouping_result.intent: Use dma_addr_t for block offset calculations to avoid address truncation in RDMA block iteration.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it replaces 32-bit block offset calculations with dma_addr_t in RDMA block iteration to prevent truncation of DMA addresses for mappings above 4G.

candidates.rationale: This 32-bit temporary held block offsets during DMA segment reassembly, so it could truncate addresses for mappings at or above 4G and lead to incorrect DMA address calculation.
This 32-bit temporary was used for offset deltas in the iterator logic, and truncation here would corrupt reconstruction of DMA addresses for large mappings.

vuln_statements.explanation: This 32-bit temporary was used to hold block offsets while reassembling DMA segments in __rdma_block_iter_next(), so mappings at or above 4G could truncate the offset and produce incorrect DMA addresses.
This 32-bit temporary was used for delta calculations in the iterator logic, and truncation of these values could corrupt the reconstructed DMA address for large IOMMU-linearized mappings.

The DMA iterator logic was mixed into verbs and umem-specific
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 6094ea64c69520ed1e770e7c79c43412de202bfa
Author: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Feb 13 12:57:37 2026 +0200

    RDMA: Move DMA block iterator logic into dedicated files
    
    The DMA iterator logic was mixed into verbs and umem-specific code,
    forcing all users to include rdma/ib_umem.h. Move the block iterator
    logic into iter.c and rdma/iter.h so that rdma/ib_umem.h and
    rdma/ib_verbs.h can be separated in a follow-up patch.
    
    Link: https://patch.msgid.
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function is exactly the DMA block iterator logic implicated by the root cause. In `__rdma_block_iter_next()`, the code uses 32-bit temporaries: `unsigned int block_offset;` and `unsigned int delta;`. It then computes them from DMA addresses with `block_offset = biter->__dma_addr & (BIT_ULL(biter->__pg_bit) - 1);` and `delta = BIT_ULL(biter->__pg_bit) - block_offset;`. Because these values are stored in `unsigned int`, offsets/deltas can truncate for mappings at or above 4G, matching the described vulnerability. There is no widened 64-bit handling or other corrective logic in this snippet, so the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet contains the vulnerable iterator logic in `__rdma_block_iter_next()`: it uses `unsigned int block_offset;` and `unsigned int delta;` while computing DMA offsets with `biter->__dma_addr = sg_dma_address(biter->__sg) + biter->__sg_advance;`, then `block_offset = biter->__dma_addr & (BIT_ULL(biter->__pg_bit) - 1);` and `delta = BIT_ULL(biter->__pg_bit) - block_offset;`.
